dose.source: 123 (finisher at the end of a front split session; no set count prescribed)

marker.label: Marker distance pushed per side; back-leg variant (wall/quad or kneeling/iliopsoas); BPM

cues: Supports either side at a height that holds you at the bottom; pad under the back knee
Slider under the front heel, marker in front of the front foot
Weaker side first
Front leg straight, hips square, separate train tracks
Escalator not elevator: hips down and forward
Up: press the back knee into the floor with the hip flexors
Feel hip flexors and hamstrings about equally
mistakes: Reaching the foot forward (twists the hips)
Twisting the hips to cheat range
progressions: Push the marker further each rep

drills.name: Blocked hip extension

dose.cr: Lift and hold 2-8 s contraction per rep
dose.source: 124: no sets/reps stated

marker.label: Block set-up (hip block height, blocks under knee, back foot elevated y/n), reps x seconds

cues: Split squat position, front knee as far over the toes as the ankle allows, hands on the front knee
Chest high and facing forward
Contact cue: hamstring to calf, or a block just under the back-leg upper thigh
Keep the contact while straightening the back knee
Squeeze the glutes almost to cramping
mistakes: Losing contact (hips lifting instead of extending)
progressions: Knee locks out fully: lower block; already lowest: elevate the back leg
regressions: Blocks under the back knee first

drills.name: Couch stretch, hips low

dose.cr: Optional: contract hard a few seconds, relax slightly, repeat (no exact seconds)
dose.source: 125: active holds mostly recommended; no numbers given

load.how_to_choose: Dumbbell over the shoulder on the back-leg side: enough to push you deeper, not so much you go less far; experiment (125)

marker.label: Dumbbell kg, method (active hold / passive hold / CR / low to high reps), seconds or reps

cues: Back foot pinned in a corner (preferred), wall or couch; pad under the knee
Hips low, torso upright
Front foot turned out 5-15 deg on its own track
Escalator not elevator
At the bottom posteriorly tilt: squeeze the back glute
progressions: Hips low to high couch stretch reps (intense)
regressions: Move the back knee further from the couch

drills.name: Couch stretch, hips high

dose.cr: Contract hard a few seconds, relax slightly; 1-3 s rest between contractions is plenty
dose.source: 126: active holds mostly recommended; no hold numbers

marker.label: Contacts reached: thigh to calf, glute to heel, lower back to wall

cues: Back foot pinned in a corner, pad under the knee, torso upright
Send the glutes toward the heel
Then posteriorly tilt: squeeze the back glute, try to touch the lower back to the wall
Good before hip-flexor focused work
regressions: Move the back knee further from the wall

drills.name: Reverse Nordic curls

dose.source: 127: no sets/reps given

load.how_to_choose: Past bodyweight: arms by sides -> on chest -> overhead

marker.label: Variant (band + ring height / object height / full BW), arm position

cues: Pad the knees
Kneel, push the hips forward and keep them extended (squeeze glutes)
Bend the knees and lean back, curve from knees to neck
progressions: Lower the band or a lighter band
regressions: Reach back to an object behind you

drills.name: Kneeling needle

dose.source: 128: reps, contract relax or longer hold; no numbers given

load.how_to_choose: Level 3: ankle weights on the straight leg

marker.label: Level (bent / straight / straight + ankle weight kg), floor or bench

cues: Forearms and knees, on the balls of the feet
Round the back to isolate the hip
Lift and squeeze hard, keep trying to lift higher
Cramping is normal: drop the leg, shake off, continue
mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift higher

drills.name: Split squats

dose.source: 134: no sets/reps given

load.how_to_choose: Learn with dumbbells, later barbell (high bar or front rack, safety pins)

marker.label: Variant + elevation height (cm, constant per phase), load type + kg, heel wedge height

cues: Legs on separate tracks, front foot turned out 5-15 deg
Back foot on the ball of the foot
Front knee far over the toes, escalator not elevator
Back leg as straight as possible
Weaker leg first, match reps on the stronger side
Grippy floor and shoes
regressions: Heel wedge under the front heel

drills.name: Rec fem pin and stretch

dose.source: 136: continue a few rounds or until improvement stops

marker.label: Before/after side photo in hips low couch stretch; spots treated; rounds

cues: Find the tight spot in a passive upright couch stretch
Lie prone on a foam roller on that spot, near body-weight pressure, no rolling
Bend the knee fully, pull the last bit with the arm, squeeze the glute into the boat position
Re-test, repeat; tightest spot first

Which is most similar to your pancake?

Training pancake for a specific sport?

pancake_phase1.frequency: Start once every 5 days; if you recover well and improve each session try every 4 days, then every 3. Poor recovery 6-7 days, average 3-5, superior 2-3. Rule: train when recovered.
notes: Doses per drill come from the 64 parameter templates (see each drill's dose).
Example program (64): A1 calf stretching forward/in/out 60 s per angle x1; B1 tailors pose 8 x 3-4 2310 60 s; C1 straddle J-curl 5 x 3-4 6240 90 s; D1 pancake lifts 6 x 2-3 1013 60 s.
Phase 2: keep going with phase 1 until progress stops (usually 4-6 weeks), then write phase 2 with the drill matrix (65) and phase 2 builder (66).
Steps: drill selection (this tree) -> program parameters (templates) -> plan phase 1 (watch each drill video).
Same straddle width every retest within a phase.

derived.formula: (er_worst + 15) - pec_worst (named on form 151; how it is used is not visible)

min over sides of eok_er_reps.reps_exact (same fallback)

149 calculator in code: push-up 1RM = bodyweight x elevation factor (flat 0.65, 30 cm 0.55, 60 cm 0.35, 90 cm 0.20) / rep factor; dip 1RM = (bodyweight + added) / rep factor; rep factor 1:1.00 2:0.95 3:0.90 4:0.87 5:0.85 6:0.83; targets push-up ER 10.70%, lower trap 11.60%, Powell 11.30%; dip ER 9.145%, lower trap 9.915%, Powell 9.658%; round 0.1
stabilisers (eok_er_worst, trap3_worst, powell_worst) under 5 reps at target, sorted ascending, take the lowest 1-2

rules.why: 151 input 10: approval to train required
141: 180 = full range, skip the other flexion tests and look at internal rotation and scapular strength; 151 also shows an 'elite range, re-check your test' message

rules.if: lat_diff > 0 (round back lower than wall) or lat_length.round_back < 180
rules.why: 143: round-back lower than flat-back = tight lats, bigger gap = tighter, full = 180 rounded; drills 155/156 target lats (pillar_lat_stretch is the alternative)
144/150: full = at least 45 deg past the shoulder line; under 15 = likely limited by pec major in shoulder sports (raise priority); 158 targets pec (157 pec_stretch_flyes = loaded alternative)

146: full = 45 past vertical; 5-10 past = minimum usable overhead (137: 15 enough for most overhead sports); short of vertical (< 0) = high priority; 160 stretches subscap/teres major (161 stick_er, 162 overhead_stick_er alternatives)
148: full = 170 from horizontal, under 135 = train this range; 164 targets IR (163 ir_contract_relax alternative, also before ER strength when the bottom range is lacking)
147 gives a yes/no result but no drill note targets pec minor specifically; flag only

rules.if: eok_er_worst < 5 and among the lowest 1-2 stabilisers
rules.why: 149: under 5 reps at target = train it, only the lowest 1-2; 160: do ER contract relax before elbow-on-knee ER

rules.if: trap3_worst < 5 and among the lowest 1-2 stabilisers
rules.why: 149 threshold; 168 trap-3 trains lower traps (start with a trap-3-only phase)

rules.if: powell_worst < 5 and among the lowest 1-2 stabilisers
rules.why: 149 threshold; 167 targets rhomboids, mid traps, rear delts

rules.if: pva_gap large (threshold not stated in notes; user-set)
rules.why: 142: active much less than passive = focus on active training; 25/28: big gap -> train the resisted end; 168: active flexibility = pauses at the top; 170/137: use horizontal/prone versions for end-range carry-over (trap3_raise_prone, er_end_range_kneeling)
142: angle the same = work on range of motion; 25/28: small gap -> push range with passive/assisted work (the stretch rules above)
165: past shoulder injury, consult a medical professional first; if cleared, start with active hangs
165: stronger but stiff -> train passive (our mapping of the form answer onto this line)
165: flexible but weak -> active (our mapping of the form answer onto this line)
151 offers 'quick ~20 min on most limiting areas': ours = keep only the highest-priority stretch rule plus the weakest stabiliser

shoulders_phase1.default_program_why: 137 recipe ends with strength-training weak patterns and adding hanging; 152 band routine as warm-up; 166 elbow-on-knee ER is 'almost always included'; 168 few people have strong enough lower traps without prior training; 165 long term use both hang types

Set targets/elevation so both sides move through the same range.

side_split.frequency: Same as pancake: start every 5 days; if you recover well and improve, every 4 days, then every 3. Poor recovery 6-7 days, average 3-5, superior 2-3. Phase 1 until progress stops, usually 4-6 weeks.
notes: Q3 slot letter depends on the path (89 says 'B, C or D depending on the path'): Q1 NO/Q2 NO -> C1 (matches the 89 example program), Q1 NO/Q2 YES -> D1, Q1 YES/Q2 NO -> B1, Q1 YES/Q2 YES -> C1.
Pancake angle (ss_pancake.angle) is only needed when the head does not touch the floor.
Example program (89): A1 Horse stance slides 10C x1 51-0 60 s; B1 Tailors pose 8 x 3-4 2310 60-90 s; B2 Horse stance squats 8 x 3-4 2310 60-90 s; C1 Standing pancake hang 6 x 2-3 C5 R5 90 s.

Side split doses for reused drills (89): Tailors pose 8 x 3-4, 2310, 60-90 s, 5-10 kg per side (depth not load). Drop stance squats 8 per side x 2-3, 2310, 45 s, weaker side first, 15 s, match reps, no weight to start, leg fully bent at the bottom. Pancake good morning 6 x 3-4, 3220, 60-90 s, 5-10 kg, do not rest at the top. Standing pancake hang 6 x 2-3, C5 R5, 90 s.

Combining with pancake (93): same session -> replace the final drill with ONE pancake drill by seated pancake: more than 45 deg standing pancake hang, less than 45 deg round back good morning (pancake_good_morning), head to floor straight arm lifts (pancake_straight_arm_lifts). Different sessions -> in the side split session answer YES to 'head touches the floor' (no pancake drills); in the pancake session answer YES to 'knees/calves touch in tailors pose'. Driven by question ss_combine_pancake; the app must apply these overrides.

Phase 2 (92): change the exercise via the drill matrix (91) or keep it and change the stimulus; one drill per group, do not use all groups, matrix order = execution order. L/R imbalance -> unilateral alternatives; no A1 needed once position is correct; tailors about 180 deg -> straight-knee adductor drills, else bent-knee; head touch / tension / 20 deg branches as phase 1 but by drill family (standing pancake, seated pancake, isometric, active, passive).

Specialist option (90): Side split overload, isometric side split hands free 40-60 s x 3, 120 s rest, 3-4x per week for 4 weeks, about 15 min, at the end of another session; warm-up 3-5 x 20 s getting wider; hold longer up to 60 s then widen; start next session at set 2 (ideally set 3) width; plateau: check recovery -> add 2.5-5 kg -> day off and retest -> new program.
Potential (95): one-off standing and prone single-leg tests to estimate potential (calves touching / flat / oversplit).

always.why: 122: one of the most bang-for-buck front split drills, targets the back-leg hip flexors; also an assessment drill (119) and the 121 specialist protocol
125: primarily a hip flexor (iliopsoas) drill for the back leg; also a front split assessment position (119)
123: trains front leg hamstrings and back leg hip flexors together; recommended as the session finisher
136: treatment technique for the rectus femoris, measured with the hips low couch stretch

rules.note: Do it before the hips low couch stretch.

rules.note: Passive split was measured open hip: keep retests open hip so results compare, or retest closed hip (the stricter version).
rules.why: 118: record closed or open hip so measurements are comparable

notes: Smith's front split builder (120) is a Jotform with hidden logic; only its inputs are known. Its hidden summary 'Front leg P vs A' (1 = work passive, 2 = work active) has no published threshold, so no passive/active rule is encoded; the metric fs_passive_vs_iso is computed for display.

Active back-leg hip extension drills (kneeling_needle 128, blocked_hip_extension 124), quad strength (reverse_nordic_curls 127) and split_squats (134) are defined for manual or later-phase selection; no note states which assessment result calls for them.
Weaker side first and match the stronger side (123, 134).

Specialist option (121): Front split overload, isometric front split hands free or lightly tapping, back leg straight, 40-60 s x 3, 120 s rest (up to 5 sets), 2-4x per week for 4 weeks, about 15 min at the end of another session; warm-up 3-5 x 20 s getting wider; every full 60 s add 2-5 cm next set; start next session at set 2 (ideally 3) width; cannot beat distance 3 sessions running -> check recovery, take the next session off; still stuck -> new program.

gaps: Pancake test hold time: note 62 says 15 s for the three seated widths but the sheet text also says hold actively for 30 s.
Seated pike (62 item 5) has no measuring rule in note 63; no measure defined.
Phase 1 Q2 does not say which straddle width (narrow, natural or maximum) decides 'most similar to your pancake'; we default to natural.
Q2 exactly 90 deg is not covered (only more than / less than 90).
Q2 in note 64 has 'chest to floor' but not 'abs to floor'; note 66 adds abs to floor. We map abs touchpoint to chest_to_floor.
Q3 (>20 deg narrow vs lift): direction of the difference not stated; we use absolute difference. The two angles use different landmarks (63 items 1-3 vs item 6).
Q3 is only defined for the >90 / <90 branches; head-to-floor and chest-to-floor already get D1 pancake lifts.
Q4 (sport) changes width only, adds no drill.
Tailors pose: Q1 in 64 asks about CALVES touching; 66 asks about KNEES (about 180 deg). Left vs right imbalance check has no measuring method beyond the total angle.
Tailors pose start load conflicts: 64 says 5-10 kg per side, 69 says about 8 kg per side minimum.
Pancake good morning load: 64 start 5-10 kg vs 75 typical 8-12 kg; 75 elevation thresholds ('40 deg or more') are unclear.
Pancake straight arm lift load: 64 says 1-2 kg total vs 77 0.5-3 kg per hand.
Straddle J-curl start: 64 5-10 kg vs 68 'titrate up from 10 kg'. No progress marker stated in 68.
Over straight arm lifts has no dedicated note or video; dose from 64 only; lesson_slug points to 77 as the nearest video.
